Headquartered in Karlskrona, PaveSight deploys vehicle-mounted stereoscopic vision arrays and real-time edge compute systems to detect potholes, rutting, and surface degradation. Our data collection methodology strictly aligns with Sweden’s official SKR standard handbook, 'Bära eller brista'. Request a Demo What is Automated Edge-Compute Infrastructure Assessment? Transforming traditional manual inspection methods into continuous 3D stereoscopic vision scanning. Why Automate Pavement Inspections Over Traditional Methods? Evaluation Criteria Traditional Subjective Inspections PaveSight Edge-Compute Scanning Inspection Speed & Frequency Manual visual surveys every 1–3 years Continuous real-time scanning on municipal fleets Measurement Precision Subjective visual ratings, high human variance Sub-centimeter 3D depth heatmaps via stereoscopic vision Operational Cost & Bandwidth High manual labor costs & expensive dedicated vans Up to 75% cost reduction with local edge computing Standardization Compliance Inconsistent scoring across municipal regions Strict alignment with SKR 'Bära eller brista' standards How Do Stereoscopic Arrays Detect Surface Defects? Vehicle Integration & Continuous Capture: Dual stereoscopic vision arrays mounted on municipal fleet vehicles continuously capture optical surface imagery during routine operations. Real-Time Edge Processing: Onboard GPU edge computing triangulates 3D stereo imagery instantly, building high-density depth heatmaps of surface defects without streaming video. Metadata Extraction & SKR Indexing: AI algorithms detect potholes, rutting, and crack depth, automatically scoring segments according to Sweden's official SKR 'Bära eller brista' handbook. Automated Geospatial Telemetry & GIS Sync: Quantified surface health metrics sync directly to municipal dashboards, enabling automated repair planning and zero-field order workflows. Challenges & Solutions in Automated Infrastructure Assessment Automated infrastructure assessment is the digital quantification of pavement condition and surface defects using sensor-equipped vehicles and real-time computing models. Transitioning from legacy manual surveys to vehicle-integrated automated systems presents distinct technical challenges. Varying environmental conditions—such as dynamic solar glare, shadows, ambient weather, and highway-speed motion blur—can obscure optical defect detection. Furthermore, streaming uncompressed 4K video feeds from municipal fleets to central cloud servers creates prohibitive cellular bandwidth costs and data latency. PaveSight solves these environmental and data transmission challenges through vehicle-mounted dual stereoscopic vision arrays coupled with onboard GPU edge computing. Stereoscopic depth triangulation measures true 3D surface geometry independent of surface shadows or lighting shifts. Simultaneously, real-time edge processing extracts sub-centimeter pothole depths, rutting measurements, and SKR 'Bära eller brista' condition scores locally on the vehicle. Only localized, anonymized vector telemetry is transmitted over cellular networks, eliminating video bandwidth costs while maintaining full GDPR privacy compliance. pages.text: About PaveSight — Founders, Technology & Operations Features Technology Insights Pricing About SE EN Dashboard Get in Contact Features Technology Insights Pricing About Dashboard Get in Contact Home / About PaveSight Transforming Municipal Infrastructure With Edge AI & Verification PaveSight AB is a leading Swedish infrastructure technology company registered in Karlskrona with operational hubs in Stockholm and Gothenburg. We empower municipalities and road contractors with real-time stereoscopic vision and edge AI road intelligence. TECHNICAL DEFINITION & SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE PaveSight AB is a leading Swedish infrastructure technology company that provides edge-compute road surface scanning by deploying vehicle-mounted stereoscopic vision arrays onto municipal utility fleets, including waste management and public service vehicles. As these vehicles navigate standard routes, PaveSight's on-device tensor processors analyze road optics in real time at up to 120 frames per second, detecting structural anomalies such as potholes, rutting (spårbildning), alligator cracking, and longitudinal degradation without transmitting raw camera feeds to external cloud servers. By executing 3D depth reconstruction directly on edge hardware, the system calculates exact defect dimensions—including depth, surface area, and required repair volume—with sub-centimeter accuracy. All collected pavement telemetry strictly conforms to "Bära eller brista," Sweden’s official SKR (Sveriges Kommuner och Regioner) handbook for municipal road condition assessment. This decentralized scanning model enables local authorities and road contractors to transition from reactive repairs to predictive maintenance while preserving full GDPR compliance. CORPORATE OVERVIEW Swedish Operations & Engineering Excellence Combining academic research with real-world infrastructure scanning. 01 Karlskrona, Stockholm & Gothenburg Presence PaveSight AB is a Swedish infrastructure technology enterprise dedicated to modernizing municipal road condition surveying and pavement maintenance. Registered with its official seat in Karlskrona and maintaining key operational hubs in Stockholm and Gothenburg, PaveSight develops continuous road intelligence solutions for public road authorities and municipal infrastructure managers. 02 Vehicle-Mounted Edge AI Our proprietary core technology combines vehicle-mounted stereoscopic vision arrays with real-time edge computing modules. Installed on existing municipal utility fleets such as waste collection trucks and public transport buses, our edge hardware continuously scans road surface optics. The system detects potholes, rutting (spårbildning), alligator cracking, and surface degradation on-the-fly without needing cloud processing. 03 SKR Handbook Alignment PaveSight’s road inspection methodology strictly complies with "Bära eller brista," the official Swedish SKR (Sveriges Kommuner och Regioner) handbook for road condition assessment. By automating pavement condition rating into standardized municipal GIS feeds, PaveSight provides objective, repeatable surface health index scores across urban and rural road networks. FIELD OPERATIONS & TESTBEDS Real-World Deployment & Operational Testbeds Proven performance alongside leading Swedish infrastructure managers and transport authorities. PROJECT EVALUATION BOLLNÄS, SE Bollnäs Field Evaluation with Svevia & Trafikverket PaveSight has been running a major real-world field evaluation project in Bollnäs involving leading infrastructure maintenance contractor Svevia and the Swedish Transport Administration ( Trafikverket ). The evaluation demonstrates continuous automated pothole detection, rutting depth measurement, and road surface profiling under harsh Swedish winter conditions. Verified by: Trafikverket • Svevia MUNICIPAL TESTBED KARLSKRONA, SE Karlskrona Municipal Road Testbed PaveSight maintains its active primary testbed on Karlskrona's road network, continuously evaluating vehicle-mounted edge-AI road surface scanning under real-world municipal operating conditions. By aligning surface defect classifications with the official SKR (Sveriges Kommuner och Regioner) "Bära eller brista" handbook, road managers gain real-time visibility into asphalt degradation. Standard Alignment: SKR Handbook "Bära eller brista" FOUNDER INSIGHT & TECHNICAL PERSPECTIVE "By executing computer vision and depth tensor inference directly on vehicle edge hardware, PaveSight eliminates the bandwidth bottlenecks and privacy risks of cloud-video streaming. This allows municipal road authorities to continuously assess pavement health with absolute objectivity, standardizing data against 'Bära eller brista' standards while maintaining 100% GDPR compliance." pages.text: Infrastructure Insights & Economics — PaveSight Features Technology Insights Pricing About SE EN Dashboard Get in Contact Features Technology Insights Pricing About Dashboard Get in Contact Home / Infrastructure Insights The Global Infrastructure Crisis The traditional "worst-first" approach to road maintenance is mathematically and economically unsustainable. €7.8B Current Scandinavian road maintenance debt (projected to double to €15.6B by 2045). 25% Sweden's national roads currently in poor condition. Root Cause Analysis Water is the catalyst. When early-stage hairline cracks are missed by infrequent surveys, moisture infiltrates the subgrade. In cold climates, water freezing and expanding by 9% rapidly creates structural voids and potholes. With PaveSight systems, these cracks can be detected and addressed before further degradation. FINANCIAL & ASSET MANAGEMENT The 1:5:25 Rule The financial models governing infrastructure heavily penalize delayed action. Pavement deterioration follows an exponential curve, meaning early intervention isn't just a best practice, it is the only way to stretch municipal budgets. 1:5 Ratio The 1:5 Ratio Every €1 not invested in preventative maintenance translates into €5 when minor rehabilitation is needed. 1:25 Ratio The 1:25 Ratio Neglecting that defect until full structural failure occurs skyrockets the cost to €25 for full-depth reconstruction. THE AI ADVANTAGE Continuous Edge Computing Replacing infrequent manual surveys with continuous, real-time AI monitoring. DECENTRALIZED SCANNING Decentralized Scanning By mounting AI-driven optical sensors on existing municipal fleets, cities transform everyday urban traffic into a continuous, real-time monitoring network. DEPTH VISUALIZATION Depth Visualization Moving beyond 2D bounding boxes, advanced AI performs pixel-level segmentation, mapping the exact irregular boundary of a defect and calculating its exact cubic volume. FIRST-TIME RIGHT DISPATCH "First-Time Right" Dispatch By automatically converting a defect's volume into the exact required mass of asphalt, crews dispatch with zero guesswork, reducing labor hours by 25% and slashing material waste by 15%. DECARBONIZATION & SUSTAINABILITY Environmental Impact 80% Less CO2 Proactive treatments emit 80% less CO2 and consume 80% less virgin aggregate than executing a full-depth road reconstruction. 12% Fuel Penalty Severe road roughness increases rolling resistance. Driving on severely deteriorated pavements can increase total fleet fuel consumption by up to 12%. 13,000 Tonnes of Microplastics Rough roads act like sandpaper on tires. Tire abrasion accounts for up to half of all primary microplastics released globally. ← Return to Home Platform Revolutionizing urban infrastructure through AI-driven, vehicle-integrated systems that detect and report road conditions in real-time.
